concepts.name: Needs versus wants
concepts.summary: Explain why spending is sorted into essentials and discretionary items and classify everyday purchases accordingly.

concepts.name: How credit cards charge interest
concepts.summary: Understand that carrying a balance incurs interest at an annual percentage rate, making purchases cost more than their price.

concepts.name: Paycheck deductions
concepts.summary: Identify the items on a pay stub, such as income tax withholding, payroll taxes and benefit contributions, that explain gross versus take-home pay.

concepts.name: Income versus expenses
concepts.summary: Distinguish gross from net income and fixed from variable expenses, and recognise that money in minus money out determines whether you save or borrow.

concepts.name: Monthly budget structure
concepts.summary: Describe how a budget assigns expected income to categories such as housing, food, savings and debt payments for a month.

concepts.name: Emergency fund purpose
concepts.summary: Explain why a cash reserve for unexpected costs prevents borrowing and covers job loss or repairs.

concepts.name: Credit score meaning
concepts.summary: Recall that a credit score summarises borrowing history and influences loan approval and interest rates.

misconceptions.text: Gross pay is the amount you have available to spend each month.
Paying only the minimum on a credit card is a fine way to pay it off.
A budget is a restriction that leaves no room for any wants.

concepts.name: Building a zero-based budget
concepts.summary: Create a monthly budget from your own net income that assigns every dollar to a category, using a framework such as 50/30/20 as a starting point.

concepts.name: Tracking spending
concepts.summary: Record and categorise actual transactions using statements or an app and compare them to the budget to find gaps.

concepts.name: Sizing an emergency fund
concepts.summary: Calculate a target of roughly three to six months of essential expenses and set a monthly contribution to reach it.

concepts.name: Paying credit cards in full
concepts.summary: Apply the statement balance, due date and grace period to avoid interest, and compute how long minimum payments take to clear a balance.

concepts.name: Credit score factors
concepts.summary: Explain how payment history, utilisation, account age, mix and new inquiries affect a score, and act on them.

concepts.name: Basic tax filing
concepts.summary: Use a W-2 and the standard deduction to complete a simple return and determine a refund or amount owed.

concepts.name: Employer retirement match
concepts.summary: Understand that contributing enough to earn an employer match gives an immediate return on those contributions.

misconceptions.text: A tax refund is a bonus rather than a return of your own overpaid money.
Carrying a small credit card balance month to month improves your credit score.
Checking your own credit score lowers it.

concepts.name: Marginal tax brackets
concepts.summary: Calculate tax under progressive brackets and distinguish marginal from effective rates when evaluating extra income.

concepts.name: Tax deductions versus credits
concepts.summary: Analyse how deductions reduce taxable income while credits reduce tax owed, and decide between standard and itemised deductions.

concepts.name: Traditional versus Roth accounts
concepts.summary: Compare when taxes are paid, contribution limits and withdrawal rules across 401(k), traditional IRA and Roth IRA accounts.

concepts.name: Insurance deductibles and premiums
concepts.summary: Analyse how premium, deductible, copay, coinsurance and out-of-pocket maximum trade off when comparing plans.

concepts.name: Compound growth in saving
concepts.summary: Apply compounding to project savings and loan balances, showing why starting early and paying interest early matter.

concepts.name: Debt payoff strategies
concepts.summary: Compare the avalanche and snowball methods for multiple debts by total interest paid and motivation, and choose one for a given situation.

concepts.name: Student loan repayment options
concepts.summary: Analyse loan types, interest accrual and repayment plans to see how each affects monthly payment and total cost.

concepts.name: Prioritising financial goals
concepts.summary: Sequence goals such as starter emergency fund, match, high-interest debt and retirement saving by their relative returns and risk.

misconceptions.text: Moving into a higher tax bracket makes all of your income taxed at the higher rate.
A tax deduction cuts your tax bill dollar for dollar.
The cheapest premium is always the cheapest insurance plan overall.

concepts.name: Tax-location of retirement savings
concepts.summary: Evaluate how to split contributions between pre-tax, Roth and taxable accounts based on current versus expected future marginal rates.

concepts.name: Refinancing and consolidation decisions
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether refinancing, consolidating or transferring a balance saves money after fees, rate changes and lost protections.

concepts.name: Insurance coverage gap analysis
concepts.summary: Analyse household exposures to find which risks to insure, retain or reduce, and size coverage such as term life and disability.

concepts.name: Risk and diversification in investing
concepts.summary: Analyse how asset allocation, diversification and fees shape risk and long-run returns within retirement accounts.

concepts.name: Retirement savings adequacy
concepts.summary: Judge whether a savings rate and balance can fund retirement using income replacement targets, inflation and sustainable withdrawal assumptions.

concepts.name: Tax-aware income planning
concepts.summary: Analyse income sources and adjust withholding or estimated payments to avoid penalties and surprises.

concepts.name: Behavioural money biases
concepts.summary: Evaluate how biases distort spending and saving decisions and judge which automation or commitment devices counter them.

misconceptions.text: Roth accounts are always better than traditional accounts regardless of your tax rate.
Refinancing to a lower monthly payment always saves money.
Insurance should cover every possible loss, however small.

concepts.name: Retirement drawdown sequencing
concepts.summary: Create a withdrawal plan that sequences taxable, pre-tax and Roth accounts and manages sequence-of-returns risk, required distributions and Social Security timing.

concepts.name: Evaluating financial advice
concepts.summary: Assess advisors, products and media claims by incentives, fees and fiduciary duty, and decide when professional help is worth its cost.

concepts.name: Multi-year tax strategy
concepts.summary: Design multi-year moves such as Roth conversions, loss harvesting and income timing that lower lifetime rather than single-year tax.

concepts.name: Stress testing household resilience
concepts.summary: Evaluate how a plan holds up under job loss, illness, inflation or market decline and judge buffers and insurance accordingly.

concepts.name: Estate and beneficiary planning
concepts.summary: Evaluate wills, beneficiary designations and powers of attorney so assets pass as intended and dependents are protected.

concepts.name: Lifetime household financial plan
concepts.summary: Design a multi-decade plan that integrates cash flow, debt, insurance, taxes, investing and retirement for a specific household.

concepts.name: Adapting plans to life events
concepts.summary: Create revised plans for events such as marriage, children, home purchase, career change or divorce, tracing the effects on every part of the plan.

misconceptions.text: A good financial plan is set once and then left unchanged.
Beneficiary designations on retirement accounts are overridden by what a will says.
A paid advisor is automatically obliged to act in your best interest.
